page: Amazon Web Services c8a.4xlarge is a compute-optimized server powered by an AMD EPYC 9R45 processor built on the x86_64 architecture. It features 16 dedicated physical cores and 16 vCPUs running at a clock speed of 4.5 GHz. The processor includes 48 KB L1d, 1.0 MB L2, and 32 MB L3 cache per core, alongside support for AVX-512 vector extensions, AVX512_vnni, AVX512_bf16, and cryptographic acceleration like AES and SHA_NI. The system is equipped with 32.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory operating at 6 GHz, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per core. It utilizes the Nitro hypervisor, includes no local storage, and provides an 8 Gbps baseline network bandwidth.

Benchmark evaluations place the c8a.4xlarge in the top tier for single-core processing, as demonstrated by stress-ng single-core CPU performance, Geekbench single-core scores, and single-threaded gzip and bzip3 operations. Multi-core performance is also highly competitive, with Geekbench multi-core scores reaching the top tier, while stress-ng multi-core and PassMark CPU scores sit in the average range. For specialized workloads, the server achieves top-tier results in image processing, text processing, and small-model LLM inference for both prompt processing and text generation. Memory bandwidth and database operations, such as Redis SET, perform within the average tier.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the c8a.4xlarge offers high compute density and modern DDR5 memory speeds without the added cost of bundled local storage or GPU hardware. This makes it a highly efficient choice for CPU-bound workloads that do not require local NVMe drives. Recommended workloads include single-threaded and multi-threaded data compression, text and image processing, static web serving, and small-scale language model inference.
